findings.title: Post id above 2**63-1 crashes update/delete with OverflowError (500) instead of 404
findings.property: unknown ids give 404, never a crash
findings.input: logged-in user, GET /9223372036854775808/update (also POST update and POST delete)
findings.expected: 404 'Post id ... doesn't exist.' as get_post documents (:raise 404: if a post with the given id doesn't exist)
findings.actual: OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to SQLite INTEGER raised in get_post (flaskr/blog.py:42); 500 in production
findings.evidence: get_post docstring: ':raise 404: if a post with the given id doesn't exist'; <int:id> accepts arbitrarily large integers, so any non-existent id should be 404.

error.message: Python int too large to convert to SQLite INTEGER

review.title: Post ids above 2**63-1 raise OverflowError (500) in get_post instead of returning 404
review.reason: The `<int:id>` converter accepts arbitrarily large integers, and `get_post` documents `:raise 404: if a post with the given id doesn't exist`. An id of 2**63 passes straight to sqlite3 as a bound parameter, which raises OverflowError, so the route returns a 500 instead of the documented 404. The input is valid for the route and the docstring promises the behaviour, so this is a real contract violation. It is a minor edge case in a tutorial example, so a maintainer might decline to complicate the code, for example by using `<int(max=...):id>` or catching OverflowError.

findings.reproSource:
def test_huge_id_is_404(client, auth):
    auth.login()
    big = 2**63
    assert client.get(f"/{big}/update").status_code == 404
    assert client.post(f"/{big}/update", data={"title": "x", "body": ""}).status_code == 404
    assert client.post(f"/{big}/delete").status_code == 404
